title: When Can Digital Personas Reliably Approximate Human Survey Findings?
abstract: arXiv:2605.10659v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Digital personas powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as substitutes for human survey respondents, yet it remains unclear when they can reliably approximate human survey findings. We answer this question using the LISS panel, constructing personas from respondents' background variables and pre-2023 survey histories, then testing them against the same respondents' held-out post-cutoff answers. Across four persona architectures, three LLMs, and two prediction tasks, we assess performance at the question, respondent, distributional, equity, and clustering levels. Digital personas improve alignment with human response distributions, especially in domains tied to stable attributes and values, but remain limited for individual prediction and fail to recover multivariate respondent structure. translated_title: 数字人格何时能可靠地近似人类调查结果？
translated_abstract: 由大语言模型驱动的数字人格日益被提议作为人类调查受访者的替代品，但它们何时能够可靠地近似人类调查结果仍不清楚。我们利用LISS面板回答这一问题：从受访者的背景变量和2023年之前的调查历史中构建数字人格，然后将其与同一受访者在截止日期之后保留的答案进行对照测试。在四种人格架构、三个大语言模型和两个预测任务中，我们在问题、受访者、分布、公平性和聚类等多个层面评估其表现。数字人格在人类回答分布的对齐上有所改善，尤其是在与稳定属性和价值观相关的领域，但在个体预测方面仍然有限，且无法恢复受访者的多变量结构。检索增强架构带来了最明显的收益，但其性能更多取决于人类回答的结构而非（模型本身）（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 基于LISS面板的研究表明，大语言模型驱动的数字人格能在分布层面较好地近似人类调查回答（尤其在涉及稳定属性和价值观的领域），但在个体预测和恢复受访者多变量结构方面仍存在根本局限。
en_tdlr: Using LISS panel data, this study finds that LLM-powered digital personas can approximate human survey response distributions—especially in domains tied to stable attributes and values—but remain limited for individual prediction and fail to recover multivariate respondent structure.
